sentences.text: Ankylosaurus is considered the largest known ankylosaurine dinosaur and possibly the largest ankylosaurid, with an estimated length of 6 to 8 meters and a weight of 4.8 to 8 metric tons.
Its skull was low, triangular, and wider than it was long, with a broad, low rear part.
This quadrupedal dinosaur had hind limbs longer than its forelimbs.
The animal wore distinctive armor made of bone knobs and plates called osteoderms embedded in its skin, which were relatively thin and reinforced by randomly distributed cushions of collagen fibers.
The tail club of Ankylosaurus seems to have been an active defensive weapon, helped by partially ossified, inelastic tail tendons that allowed great force to be transmitted.
A 2009 study estimated that large tail clubs could generate enough force to break bones on impact, but medium and small ones could not.
Ankylosaurus became the best-known ankylosaur in popular culture, possibly due to a life-sized reconstruction at the 1964 World's Fair in New York City.
The genus Ankylosaurus was named by Barnum Brown in 1908.
The type specimen of Ankylosaurus magniventris was discovered in 1906 by Barnum Brown in the Hell Creek Formation near Gilbert Creek, Montana.
Other Ankylosaurus fossils have been found in Wyoming, Alberta, and Saskatchewan.
Only a few Ankylosaurus specimens have been found, and no complete skeleton has been discovered yet.
Ankylosaurus was a herbivore, like other ornithischian dinosaurs.
It likely fed as a non-selective browser, indicated by its broad muzzle.
It is believed to have been a slow animal capable of making quick movements when necessary.
Paleontologist Walter P. Coombs suggested ankylosaurs may have been capable diggers, though limited by their hoof-like hands.
Researchers believe Ankylosaurus used its tail club for defense against predators or in fights with other Ankylosaurus.
The Ankylosaurus tail club was semicircular from above, distinguishing it from the pointed clubs of Anodontosaurus and the narrow clubs of Dyoplosaurus.
The U-shaped zygapophyses and neural spines of Ankylosaurus tail vertebrae differ from the V-shape of most other ankylosaurids, possibly due to a wider tail handle.
The blunter squamosal horns in larger Ankylosaurus specimens compared to smaller ones may represent ontogenetic variation.
In 1977, Teresa Maryańska proposed ankylosaur sinuses may have lightened the skull, housed a gland, or aided vocal resonance.
In 1969, Georg Haas concluded that ankylosaur skull musculature was relatively weak despite the large skull size.
Ankylosaurus belongs to the family Ankylosauridae, with Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus as its closest relatives.
Henry Fairfield Osborn named the suborder Ankylosauria in 1923.
Ankylosaurus lived between 68 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period.
Ankylosaurus likely inhabited upland areas, and its ecological niche does not seem to have overlapped with that of the nodosaurid Denversaurus.
The clade Thyreophora, which includes Ankylosaurus, existed from the Sinemurian age until the Maastrichtian, spanning 135 million years.
The rarity of Ankylosaurus fossils suggests it was ecologically rare or restricted to uplands where fossilization was less likely.

In 2015, Arbour and Currie disputed Kenneth Carpenter's reconstruction of the Ankylosaurus neck armor, noting that the holotype fragments did not fit his proposed arrangement, though breakage might explain the discrepancy.
Carpenter rejected the idea that ankylosaur sinuses aided vocalization or significantly reduced skull weight.
